content: Individuals with diabetes are at an increased risk of developing heart failure, even if they do not exhibit any symptoms. Research indicates that diabetes is associated with a higher prevalence of structural abnormalities in the heart, which can predispose individuals to heart failure. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends enhanced screening for heart failure in patients with diabetes who are considered high-risk. Specific biomarkers, such as NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide), are valuable tools for the early identification of these high-risk individuals. Studies have demonstrated that early monitoring for the development of heart failure in this population can provide significant benefits, including a reduction in the risk of hospitalizations and a decrease in mortality rates among high-risk patients.
